title: Eventual compatible refinement of finite local unit lifts
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], J a small cofiltered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and D:J→X_et a diagram of etale objects [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] whose terms are affine [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and whose structure maps to X are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let c be a limiting cone of the underlying scheme diagram and p:c.pt→X satisfy c.π_j followed by D(j).hom = p for every j. Let H be a left adjoint to p_* with specified adjunction hH [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], F an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and t a section of H(F) on the terminal etale object T=(c.pt,id). Write p* for actual base change [def-pc-fibre-product] and η for the specified adjunction unit. Fix a stage j, a finite possibly empty set B, affine etale X-objects V_b, a covering v_b:V_b→D(j), sections s_b in F(V_b), and a covering π_b:p*V_b→T with H(F)(π_b)(t)=η_F(V_b)(s_b). There exist k, f:k→j, etale X-objects V′_b, arrows v′_b:V′_b→D(k), γ_b:V′_b→V_b and π′_b:p*V′_b→T such that v′_b followed by D(f) equals γ_b followed by v_b; both v′ and π′ are covering families; p*(γ_b) followed by π_b equals π′_b; and the restrictions F(γ_b)(s_b) are compatible: for every etale X-object W and arrows a:W→V′_b, a′:W→V′_b′ with a followed by v′_b equal to a′ followed by v′_b′, their further restrictions to W are equal. No global section or amalgamation is asserted.

proof.text: For each ordered pair of indices apply pair_eventual_agreement to the two sections and their common terminal inverse-image section. This produces one stage and a test-object equality criterion for each pair.

Apply Mathlib IsCofiltered.wideCospan to the finite family of arrows to j. This gives a common stage k, a map f:k→j and maps to every pair stage commuting with those arrows. This also works for the empty family.

At this fixed k and f apply refinement_data. For two test arrows with equal composites to D(k), compose their maps to the original V objects with the covering projections. The refinement-square equations and the wide-cospan equations put them under the equality criterion for that pair. Presheaf functoriality rewrites that equality as the required compatibility of restricted sections.

theorem affineOpenSections_inverse_image_compatible_refinement
    {X : Scheme.{u + 1}} {J : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (D : J ⥤ X.Etale)
    [∀ j, IsAffine (D.obj j).left] [∀ j, IsOpenImmersion (D.obj j).hom]
    (c : Cone (D ⋙ Scheme.Etale.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X))
    (p : c.pt ⟶ X) (hp : ∀ j, c.π.app j ≫ (D.obj j).hom = p)
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    (H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⥤
      Sheaf c.pt.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hH : H ⊣ p.Etale.sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} X.smallEtaleTopology c.pt.smallEtaleTopology)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (t : (H.obj F).obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 c.pt))))
    (j : J) (B : Type (u + 1)) [Finite B]
    (V : B → X.Etale) (v : ∀ b, V b ⟶ D.obj j)
    (s : ∀ b, F.obj.obj (op (V b)))
    (π : ∀ b, p.Etale.obj (V b) ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 c.pt))
    (hV : ∀ b, IsAffine (V b).left)
    (hv : Sieve.ofArrows V v ∈ X.smallEtaleTopology (D.obj j))
    (hπ : Sieve.ofArrows (fun b ↦ p.Etale.obj (V b)) π ∈
      c.pt.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 c.pt)))
    (hs : ∀ b, (H.obj F).obj.map (π b).op t =
      (hH.unit.app F).hom.app (op (V b)) (s b)) :
    ∃ (k : J) (f : k ⟶ j) (V' : B → X.Etale)
      (v' : ∀ b, V' b ⟶ D.obj k) (γ : ∀ b, V' b ⟶ V b)
      (π' : ∀ b, p.Etale.obj (V' b) ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 c.pt)),
      (∀ b, v' b ≫ D.map f = γ b ≫ v b) ∧
      Sieve.ofArrows V' v' ∈ X.smallEtaleTopology (D.obj k) ∧
      Sieve.ofArrows (fun b ↦ p.Etale.obj (V' b)) π' ∈
        c.pt.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 c.pt)) ∧
      (∀ b, p.Etale.map (γ b) ≫ π b = π' b) ∧
      ∀ ⦃W : X.Etale⦄ ⦃b b' : B⦄ (a : W ⟶ V' b) (a' : W ⟶ V' b'),
        a ≫ v' b = a' ≫ v' b' →
        F.obj.map a.op (F.obj.map (γ b).op (s b)) =
          F.obj.map a'.op (F.obj.map (γ b').op (s b'))
